criteria.name: Introduction: mission concept and rationale - Include the following required information: • What is the spacecraft's primary mission? • Why is the mission needed? • How many spacecraft are used and why? • Who are the users (operator and customers)?
criteria.reasoning: Covers primary mission (coral reef/ocean monitoring via fluid lensing), rationale (bleaching, GBR), single-spacecraft justification, and users (CSIRO/BOM, government/university). References [1]-[4] support claims. Detailed and persuasive, though some referencing is weak.

evidence.quote: The spacecraft is intended to image and send data to ground stations for collation and analysis.
governmental and science agencies (e.g. CSIRO, BOM)

criteria.name: Main body: mission design - Present a summary of the mission design using software and/or hand calculations as appropriate - Include relevant screenshots and software files (in the main body of the report and/or appendix) - Include the following information: • Where it will launch from, and using which launch vehicle? Why did you choose this option? • What type of orbit will you use? What are its characteristics and orbital elements? • Will you need to perform any orbital maneuvers? • Which ground control facilities will you use? • How often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control? • How long will the mission last, and what are your plans for EOL?
criteria.reasoning: Addresses launch, orbit, ground station, duration and EOL with STK screenshots and an inclination plot. But launch vehicle is unflown, Kourou-to-SSO dogleg ignored, access table has duplicate/inconsistent rows, no link budget, no software files, and Wikipedia used for launch data. Errors and missing detail place it at Adequate.

evidence.quote: an altitude of 600km requires a mean inclination of 97.7924° for the satellite to remain sun-synchronous.
The proposed satellite will thus use the Vega E rocket as a launch vehicle – launched from the Guiana Space Centre Spaceport.
An average contact duration of almost ten minutes was achieved

criteria.name: Conclusion
criteria.reasoning: Reaches specific conclusions on launch, orbit and ground station, but omits mission duration and EOL outcomes, and is somewhat generic. Adequate but not detailed.

evidence.quote: A polar sun-synchronous orbit allows for consistent illumination of the oceans while maintaining a constant sun angle.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Clear structure with headings and readable prose, but grammar errors ('a Earth', 'complied', 'purposed'), figures lack numbers, tables unlabelled, bibliography is bare URLs, and Wikipedia is cited. Presentation is adequate but not professional.

evidence.quote: STK 3D view of orbit: 12 hours apart

technical_issues.issue: Vega E is not yet operational (first launch 2024) and may not be available for 2025; launch from Kourou (5.05°N) to a 97.79° retrograde SSO requires a significant dogleg/plane change not discussed. Claim of 'two launch windows per day' is questionable.

RAAN 27.33° is said to indicate launch facility location; RAAN is not directly set by site latitude/longitude but by launch azimuth and time. No orbit maintenance (drag, J2) or station-keeping discussed.
STK access table contains a duplicate row 15 and row 6 has a 24-hour span but 365 s duration, indicating data inconsistency. No link budget or data-rate analysis.
Drag sail is proposed but not sized, and no demonstration of compliance with 25-year deorbit rule or deployment mechanism.
References are bare URLs without author/title/date; Wikipedia is used as a source [6], violating the no-Wikipedia requirement.
Figures have captions but no figure numbers; tables (launch, orbital elements, access) are unlabelled with table numbers/titles.

overall: A competent but flawed report. It covers all major mission elements with STK evidence and a coherent design, but technical gaps (launch dogleg, unflown vehicle, table errors, no link budget) and weak referencing/presentation reduce the mark. Weighted average approximately 6/10.

feedback.summary: Overall, your report is competent but flawed: it covers all major mission elements with STK evidence and a coherent design, but technical gaps (launch dogleg, unflown vehicle, table errors, no link budget) and weak referencing/presentation reduce the mark. Focus next on resolving launch/orbit consistency, adding link-budget/table accuracy and software files, and fixing presentation/referencing.
next_steps: Resolve launch/orbit consistency: justify Vega E availability or choose an operational vehicle; discuss the Kourou-to-SSO dogleg/plane change and correct the 'two launch windows per day' claim.
Add a link budget/data-rate analysis and clean the STK access table (remove duplicate row 15, fix row 6 inconsistency); include software files and size the drag sail with 25-year deorbit compliance.
Fix presentation and referencing: number figures and label tables, replace bare URLs with full citations, remove Wikipedia [6], and proofread grammar (e.g. 'a Earth', 'complied', 'purposed').

criteria.C1: Your Introduction clearly states the coral-reef/ocean monitoring mission, rationale (bleaching/GBR), single-spacecraft justification, and users (CSIRO/BOM, government/university), supported by [1]–[4]. To strengthen toward the top of Accomplished, tighten weak referencing and ensure every claim has a specific source.
criteria.C2: Your Mission Design addresses launch, orbit, ground control, duration and EOL with STK screenshots and an inclination plot. Gaps noted: Vega E is unflown; Kourou-to-SSO dogleg/plane change is not discussed; STK access table has duplicate row 15 and inconsistent row 6; no link budget/data-rate analysis; software files missing; Wikipedia used for launch data. For Accomplished, resolve these and support all major requirements with quality evidence (software files, hand calculations, literature).
criteria.C3: Your Conclusion reaches specific points on launch, orbit and ground station, e.g. the polar SSO rationale. However, it omits mission duration and EOL outcomes and is somewhat generic. To reach Accomplished, draw detailed and appropriate conclusions from all evidence in the report, including duration, EOL/deorbit compliance, and communications performance.
criteria.C4: Your report has clear headings and readable prose, but grammar errors ('a Earth', 'complied', 'purposed'), figures lack numbers, tables are unlabelled, bibliography is bare URLs, and Wikipedia is cited [6]. To reach Accomplished, provide a professional engineering report structure: consistent formatting, numbered/labelled figures and tables, proofread language, and full citations matching the reference list with no Wikipedia.
